title: Introduce sparse-span correlator and epochal cost dashboard
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Added sparse-span correlator for low-cardinality trace joins and a new epochal cost dashboard for burst-cost investigation. No breaking API changes.
description: Context: We've been seeing a class of long-tail cost incidents where expensive token-paths only show up in very sparse traces (1-5 spans) and are missed by current reservoir or percentile rollups. This PR introduces a lightweight 'sparse-span correlator' which attaches a small, privacy-safe fingerprint to traces that surfaces correlated cost/latency anomalies across epochs, plus a dashboard and query primitives to inspect epochal cost distributions. Motivation: improve detection of recurring high-cost token patterns that don't produce large-span traces and therefore evade sampling-heavy rollups. Goals: 1) surface recurring sparse anomalies for on-call and SRE, 2) enable fast grouping of epochs (24h/7d) to prioritize model/route-level investigation, 3) avoid increasing cardinality in the primary metrics tables. Design summary: - Sparse-span correlator: hash-based, deterministic 64-bit fingerprint computed from a stable canonicalization of the request path and first-k tokens (k configurable, default 8) with per-tenant salt. The fingerprint is emitted as an indexed label on a small auxiliary metric stream (sparse_span.fingerprint) and as an otel resource attribute on sampled spans. - Epochal cost dashboard: pre-aggregated daily and hourly rollups keyed by (route, model_variant, fingerprint) with a compact 'burst score' that weights recent epochs higher. The dashboard includes a lightweight cohort explorer that shows the top fingerprints by burst score, token-cost histogram for the cohort, and span-minimap for exemplar traces. - Sampling and cardinality strategy: We avoid increasing primary metric cardinality by keeping fingerprinted metrics in a secondary rollout table backed by TTL and reservoir deduplication. Only fingerprints that exceed a configured burst_score or that are manually flagged are promoted to the main token-cost rollups. - Privacy and security: fingerprints are non-reversible hashes with tenant salt; we validate that the canonicalization removes user-specific fields (email, PII) before hashing. Implementation highlights: commits contain the correlator library in /pkg/observability/correlator, ingestion hooks for the collector, a lightweight ClickHouse schema for the fingerprint rollups, Grafana dashboard JSON, and an integration test harness that replays synthetic sparse-anomaly workloads. Testing and validation: - Unit tests: correlator deterministic hashing, canonicalizer sanitization, and promotion logic. - Integration: replayed 3 synthetic incident traces over the last 90 days into a staging cluster; dashboard shows consistent fingerprint cohorts and burst_score trend. - Load testing: ingestion hook benchmarked to add ~2.1% CPU on a 32-core collector at 50k req/s with default k=8. Deployment plan and rollouts: feature gated behind observability.sparse_span_enabled. Early rollout to internal org and a small set of customers flagged via feature flags. Promotion to wide rollout after 2 weeks of stable metrics and no privacy concerns. Checklist: - [x] correlator core library implemented - [x] collector hook and ingest path - [x] ClickHouse schema and TTL rollups - [x] Grafana dashboard and panels - [x] unit/integration tests - [x] docs draft in observability-playbook - [x] feature flag gating - [x] SRE runbook stub included Backwards compatibility and risk: The change is read-only for existing tracing; new metrics only emitted when the feature flag is enabled. Risk areas: incorrect canonicalization could leak PII (mitigated by sanitization tests), increased collector CPU (mitigated by k and sampling knobs). Follow-ups (post-merge): - ENG-4610: Add automated churn detection to avoid fingerprint pollution from transient tokens - ENG-4688: Expose an API for customers to request fingerprint suppression for regulated tenants - Dashboard UX follow-ups: add cohort comparison view and CSV export Review summary: - Ben: requested more explicit sanitization assertions in unit tests and a short doc on non-reversibility of fingerprints; addressed in commit 4. - Ivy: asked for clearer default knobs for k and TTL; added configuration defaults and documented expected CPU delta. - Samir: asked about query perf for large numbers of fingerprints; added reservoir dedup and promotion flow, plus ClickHouse indexing recommendations. CI: All unit/integration tests passed in CI, linting fixed after one CI rerun. The Grafana JSON validates against our panel schema. Merge: Squash-merged after approvals and a green CI run. Notes for on-call: runbook added under docs/sre/runbooks/sparse-span-correlator.md with mitigation steps, query snippets, and a rollback flag to disable emission at collector level.
